## Goal
Improve Firstmate 3000’s Tasks and card UI, stop disruptive keychain prompts, fix Claude’s recurring startup Retry, and make GitHub-dependent work offer sign-in when needed.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Keep distinct requests as separate tasks; use proposed changes for `firstmate-3000` (autonomy off).
- Avoid entering passwords, exposing secrets, or triggering unnecessary keychain prompts.
- In card threads, show only “working”—no animated crewmate glyph. A card’s X should close the whole card even when chat is expanded.

## Progress
### Done
- [x] Cloned `https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate-3000` as repo `daf07048`.
- [x] Merged Tasks section arrows (#297), concise Activity notes (#296), routine-install keychain fix (#298), Dock GitHub-tool lookup (#299), active parent-tree grouping (#301), card-thread working indicator (#302), task-key prefixes (#303), reply-time card hiding (#304), and expanded Tasks header layout (#305).
- [x] Closed the earlier Claude startup investigation without a supported fix; a later restart reproduced the problem.
- [x] Reproduced the expanded-chat X bug and the missing GitHub sign-in handoff.

### In Progress
- [ ] FI3-36 `d9b06d9b`: recurring Claude Retry fix is committed; awaiting GitHub delivery.
- [ ] FI3-42 `3d3d024d`: replace the card-thread animated glyph with text-only “working.”
- [ ] FI3-45 `0553d962`: make X close the whole card; local checks passed, delivery awaits GitHub access.
- [ ] FI3-39 `d680700b`: GitHub sign-in handoff is awaiting the captain’s choice on card `card-fm-2-baf50b`.
- [ ] FI3-33 `45c42357`: local signing secret unlock issue remains charted, starts on request.
- [ ] FI3-47 `c1daf6ae`: separate sequence card-thread reply-test failure remains charted.

### Blocked
- The captain chose **“Connect GitHub sign-in”** on `card-fm-3-ab2261`, but completion of sign-in is not yet confirmed. Repo context still says `github (not signed in)`.
- FI3-39 found that direct crewmate git failures bypass the model-provider auth gate. `WorkspaceService.dispatchBase` reduces fetch exceptions to plain `fetchError` via `gitFailure`, losing typed auth cause, remote, and retry operation. The captain has not yet chosen whether to build the broader handoff.
- A live-main check for FI3-33 was not verified: the crewmate inspected cached `origin/main` at `e2b0893`, not a freshly fetched server head.

## Key Decisions
- **GitHub handoff proposal**: On a *confirmed* GitHub-auth-required failure for a known project, pause the affected task, offer Projects GitHub sign-in, then retry it. Do not classify generic network failures as authentication failures.
- **Claude Retry diagnosis**: The installed app’s Developer ID requirement matches the saved item’s ordinary ACL, but a separate macOS partition rule allowed Apple tools and refused the app. FI3-36 implemented a fallback confined to unlocked Claude items whose metadata verifies the existing Apple-tool permission; it does not edit the ACL.
- **Signing follow-up**: The routine-install fix avoids unlocking an already-matching dev signature, but missing/changed signatures and local packaging still require the saved signing password. FI3-33 is not known to be obsolete.

## Next Steps
1. Confirm whether GitHub sign-in completed after the captain’s choice; then resume FI3-45 and FI3-36 delivery without opening duplicate sign-in cards.
2. Await the captain’s choice on `card-fm-2-baf50b` before expanding FI3-39 into a typed sign-in-and-resume flow.
3. Finish and validate FI3-42 and FI3-45; bring proposed changes to captain decisions once checks pass.
4. Keep FI3-33 and FI3-47 separate unless the captain requests them.

## Critical Context
- Repo path: `/Users/captain/Library/Application Support/firstmate-3000/fleet/firstmate-3000`; bundled source: `/Applications/Firstmate 3000.app/Contents/Resources/self-source`.
- GitHub failure evidence: `unable to read askpass response`; `could not read Username ... terminal prompts disabled`. The exact earlier live-main lookup failure was not independently established until a later worker fetch produced this askpass error.
- FI3-45’s isolated Playwright regression showed clicking the right-hand X left one card layer instead of zero; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm lint:adherence`, build, and isolated regression subsequently passed locally.
- FI3-42’s target is `WorkingRow` in `src/renderer/src/cards/CardThread.tsx`: retain `data-thread-working`, `aria-busy="true"`, and activity logic; remove canvas, animation, and “crew” prefix.
- FI3-36’s full local test run had four unrelated local-signing failures. The separate sequence-flow reply test timed out awaiting an acknowledgment after 30 seconds; FI3-47 tracks it.

<addendum>
# Sequences

How I want work of each kind approached. Open a new ask as a parent task and its steps as
child tasks; name each step by its kind (plan, research, reproduce, implement, fix); spawn
each step when its turn comes; if I say "just do it", skip the plan. Validation is the
project's rigor and happens inside the implement or fix step; it is never a step of its
own. Each step you add yourself is an internal step: say so when you create it
(internal_step), and once the next step has started, close it as answered. An answer I ask
for myself is never an internal step - a plan, a reproduction, some research, or a step's
result I asked to see ("show me the repro first"): it shows its answer as a card, it is
mine to close, and the next step starts on my choice there. The parent completes when its
last step lands.

## ideation - deciding what to do
- plan: a read-only step. Research the code and the field, then propose two or three
  directions as one card when it is ambiguous, with the one you would take as the default.
  Revise it on my replies until I choose. Each time it changes, write the full agreed spec
  into the task as its report - my tweaks and anything decided on the card included - so
  the step that builds on it starts from that recorded spec.

## feature - building something new, or an unclear ask
- plan: as above; wait for my choice
- implement: on request. Start it when I accept, grounded on the plan (basis) - its
  recorded spec and my choice - from the plan's branch if it has one. The simplest change
  that meets the accepted plan.

## bugfix - something is broken
- reproduce: a read-only step. Reproduce it as reported, in a clean setup, and put the
  failing check in the report. Open your report with "reproduced: yes" or "reproduced: no".
- fix: on request. On "reproduced: yes" start it grounded on the reproduction (basis), then
  close the reproduce step as answered; on "reproduced: no" ask me first. The smallest
  root-cause fix; it adds the failing check and makes it pass.

## refactor - changing structure, not behaviour
- implement: one step. First establish the right guardrails: prove the coverage of what the
  refactor touches and add what is missing until it passes; then do the refactoring under
  them.

## explainer - understanding something
- research: a read-only step; one card, drawn, revised on my questions
</addendum>

toolsAdded.name: close_card
toolsAdded.description: Withdraw a card of YOUR OWN that is no longer valid or necessary, without waiting for the captain. A note may be closed freely when stale, except a note you emitted as this turn's answer is current and must not be withdrawn during this turn. Close a decision only when the choice no longer applies - you are withdrawing it as obsolete, not answering for the captain. Pass the card id returned by emit_card. Only the card's own author may close it: Firstmate its own cards (card-fm-...), a crewmate the cards it emitted. Someone else's card is not yours to close - steer its author instead; the captain dismisses a card himself. Unknown ids fail loudly.

card_id.description: The open card's id, as returned by emit_card

reason.description: Why this card is obsolete; one line

toolsAdded.name: emote
toolsAdded.description: Make the Firstmate character perform one brief emote. Use this for a fitting visible acknowledgement when no card is needed; it is visual only and does not replace required work or a card. greet: hello. celebrate: good news. ponder: thinking it over. confused: something went wrong. fidget: idle play. The reply emotes play as your turn ends: nod - got it, an instruction understood; salute - on it, work sent out; tick - all set, a change you made yourself; tuck - noted, something kept; aww - any time, the captain's thanks or praise. On a captain turn the app already nods for a steer you deliver, tucks for a note you keep and ticks for a personalize you apply.

emote.description: The supported character emote to perform

toolsAdded.name: steer_crewmate
toolsAdded.description: Send guidance, feedback, or a follow-up to a crewmate's running or idle task. The data plane only - use interrupt_crewmate for lifecycle control. Some crewmates cannot take guidance mid-turn; the result says so when the message was queued for their next turn instead.

task_id.description: The task id from the context block or spawn

message.description: What the crewmate should know or do next

toolsAdded.name: interrupt_crewmate
toolsAdded.description: Lifecycle control for a task. mode 'interrupt' stops the current turn but keeps the crewmate steerable; mode 'cancel' ends the task. Never send lifecycle instructions as steer text.

task_id.description: The task id

toolsAdded.name: crew_status
toolsAdded.description: Fresh structured state of the crew - one task or all. Authoritative over your memory: always check here before steering or re-escalating.

task_id.description: One task id; omit for the whole crew

toolsAdded.name: update_task
toolsAdded.description: Edit a task's record: title, goal, priority, start_policy, parent (a task id or key, or an empty string to clear), or project (a project key; only open work that has not started can move). To drop a task pass drop true with reason: an open row closes as dropped, and a parent with open children needs confirm true, which drops them too as superseded. Work a crewmate holds is settle_task's business, never dropped here. To start a queued task right now pass start_now true: it dispatches at once, on whatever model has quota, past a wait on a reasoning class that has none. Refusals come back as text: read them, they name the tasks in the way.

start_policy.description: when-ready: starts on its own once nothing blocks or holds it; on-request: waits for the user's go

parent.description: New parent (task id or key); empty string clears it

project.description: Move to this project (key from the tasks index)

start_now.description: Start a queued task right now on whatever model has quota, past a reasoning-class wait

reason.description: Why it is dropped (required with drop)

confirm.description: Required to drop a parent with open children after the captain chose

toolsAdded.name: link_tasks
toolsAdded.description: Record a typed edge between two tasks (ids or keys). blocks: `to` cannot start until `from` closes - a cycle is refused as text. related: informational. discovered-from: `from` was found while doing `to`. Pass remove true to unlink.

from.description: The task the edge starts at (id or key)

to.description: The task the edge points at (id or key)

toolsAdded.name: tasks
toolsAdded.description: Query the task record: compact rows with key, task_id, kind, status, title, project, parent, blockers, what it blocks, children, and whether it is ready or what it waits on. Filter by project (key), status (open, active, done, dropped, live, closed), key (one task), text (title or goal), or parent (its children). Fetch one task by key to read its report and its last card; a list stays compact and carries neither. The context block's tasks index is a bounded view of the same record; this is the full one.

project.description: A project key from the tasks index

status.description: live = open, active; closed = done, dropped

key.description: One task by key or id

parent.description: List the children of this task

toolsAdded.name: check_pr_ci
toolsAdded.description: Typed CI status for a task's open PR: every check on the PR head SHA, plus an overall verdict - green only when every check is completed and successful; one green job never suffices while others pend or fail. Call it before any land or merge decision on a direct-pr task: a land decision card is refused without a fresh green result. Not green: steer the crewmate to fix and re-report.

task_id.description: The task id from crew_status or the context block

toolsAdded.name: setup_repo
toolsAdded.description: Bring a repository under fleet management so crewmates can work on it (worktree per task). Setting up is your job, never the user's: do it in the turn they ask, choosing the kind from their intent. kind clone fetches a remote (pass origin) into the fleet root; kind init creates a brand-new project (pass name) there; kind adopt manages an existing local folder (pass its absolute path) in place - the folder never moves, the fleet root gains a link, and a folder that is not yet a git repository is initialized. Setting up something already managed just returns the existing entry.

origin.description: clone: the remote URL to clone from

path.description: adopt: absolute path of the existing local folder

name.description: init: the new project's name; optional override for clone/adopt

toolsAdded.name: configure_repo
toolsAdded.description: Change a managed repo's delivery posture, autonomy flag, and/or standing rigor. delivery direct-pr ships finished work as a pushed branch plus a pull request; local-only lands it on a local branch and never leaves the machine (the personal workspace is a workspace kind, not a posture: delivery, autonomy, and rigor cannot be set on it). autonomy true lets you land green finished work on the repo yourself; false (the default) means you surface the decision instead. rigor is how carefully every crewmate on the repo ships: quick, standard, or reviewed (an independent reviewer holds each merge until it passes); default returns the repo to the host's own derivation per task. Pass it only when the user said in words how careful this repository should be.

repo_id.description: A managed repo id from the context block

toolsAdded.name: unregister_repo
toolsAdded.description: Remove a repository from fleet management. Its data is never deleted: an adopted repo just loses its fleet link, a cloned or created repo's directory stays on disk. Refused while tasks are still queued or running on it - settle the crew there first.

repo_id.description: A managed repo id from the context block

toolsAdded.name: schedule_prompt
toolsAdded.description: Schedule a prompt to be delivered back to you later, as an [fm-op] - for recurring checks or a one-time reminder. Pass exactly one of every_minutes (recurring, 15 minimum), daily_at (HH:MM local), or at_time (ISO 8601). The prompt should carry everything future-you needs. Fires only while the app runs; missed fires run once at the next launch, flagged as catch-up.

prompt.description: The prompt delivered to you at each fire

toolsAdded.name: cancel_schedule
toolsAdded.description: Cancel a schedule by its id (active schedules are listed in the context block).

toolsAdded.name: supervision_log
toolsAdded.description: Read the durable log of routine fleet events already triaged on your behalf: each task, verdict, and summary, newest first. Use it when the user asks what happened in the fleet.

recent.description: How many most-recent outcomes to read (default 20)

toolsAdded.name: flag_missed_escalation
toolsAdded.description: Record that a fleet event triaged as routine should have reached the user. Call it only after the user says something was missed AND you have checked supervision_log and confirmed the event was handled routinely. Never call it on a hunch, on your own initiative, or for an event that did reach the user. It writes a label and nothing else: no card, no message, no change to the task.

task_id.description: The task whose routine outcome was the miss

what_was_missed.description: In the user's own terms, what should have been raised and why

outcome_id.description: The supervision_log outcome id (#N) when a specific one is meant; otherwise the task's most recent routine outcome is labelled

toolsAdded.name: flag_duplicate
toolsAdded.description: Record that a card repeats an earlier card, and close it. Call it only when the user says a card duplicates another one; pass the duplicate's card id and the id of the earlier card it repeats, from the context block or the on-screen hint. Never call it on your own initiative or to tidy the stack - close_card is for that. It writes a label and closes the duplicate: no card, no message.

duplicate_of.description: The id of the earlier card it repeats

note.description: The user's words on why it is a duplicate

toolsAdded.name: remember
toolsAdded.description: Save a durable note that survives compaction and restarts. Use when the user states a preference, correction, or personal detail. Kinds: preference (write as an imperative directive: Always/Never/Prefer, not an observation), fact, lesson. Scope is captain (default) or a repo_id from the context block; it cannot change later. Pass a kebab-case id and reuse it to revise. Evidence is required: why this is true. Do not re-save a note already in the context; revise it. Skip trivia, raw dumps, task progress, and TODOs. Intentions are not notes: use schedule_prompt or a queued task. Scheduled and escalated turns may revise but must not create.

id.description: Stable kebab-case id (squash-merges). Reuse to revise the same note.

evidence.description: Why this is true: the user's words or the report it was distilled from

scope.description: captain (default) or a repo_id from the context block

toolsAdded.name: forget
toolsAdded.description: Retire a durable note by id. History is kept; the note leaves the context. Evidence is required. Use when the user says to forget, or when live state contradicts the note.

id.description: The note id from the context block

evidence.description: Why this note is no longer true or wanted

toolsAdded.name: spawn_crewmate
toolsAdded.description: Commission a crewmate for project work or an evidence-gathering investigation. Pass a structured intent - a one-sentence goal, the user's words verbatim (they outrank every elaboration downstream), typed constraints, and an optional delivery note - and the crewmate, a strong model, briefs itself from it on its first turn. Do not author a brief. Pass repo_id from the context block to bind a managed repository; omit it for repo-less work (the default workspace). An ask about the user's own panels on the rails - a new one, or a change to a surface the context block lists - is personal_ui true: the host binds the personal workspace itself (no repo_id) and the crewmate builds in place, so name the existing surface's id in the goal for a change. Returns the task id immediately; the crewmate's results arrive later as [fm-op] messages, so end your turn.

goal.description: One sentence: what done looks like, in plain language

user_words.description: The user's request verbatim; outranks every elaboration downstream

repo_id.description: A registered repo id from the context block

personal_ui.description: True when the ask is about the user's own panels on the rails; the host binds the personal workspace, so omit repo_id

kind.description: read-only: the task answers a question and changes nothing, so it commits nothing, pushes nothing and opens no pull request; tests-required; no-new-deps; minimal-diff; free: anything else, relayed verbatim

text.description: Required when kind is free; optional qualifier otherwise

constraints.description: Typed constraint flags plus free strings

delivery_note.description: A delivery expectation refining the repository posture, e.g. "stack on top of PR 41". A posture override is delivery_ask, not this.

delivery_ask.description: Only when the user asked in words for this task to ship as a PR or to stay local; omit otherwise. The host uses it for this task alone; the repository's default is unchanged.

basis.description: The task (id or key) whose report is this work's spec, or whose reproduction it fixes. Name it only when that task really carries the plan, spec, or reproduction - the host checks it, and an unverified basis is ignored. Omit when the work starts from nothing.

premium_ask.description: True only when the user asked for a premium or the best model in words. Never your own judgment.

override_model_id.description: An exact model id to pin this task to (e.g. gpt-6-astra), or a provider-qualified Pi key (e.g. anthropic-claude/claude-fable-5-1) when the provider matters. Use it only when the user named a model; it wins over everything else when currently available and otherwise falls back to normal routing.

escalate_from.description: The task (id or key) whose result the user just rejected in words. Set it only on a turn where the user themselves said the result is wrong, asked for a better or smarter attempt, or rejected a completion - never on a crewmate's own report that it is blocked, and never on an operational wake. The host stops that attempt, keeps its branch, runs this fresh crewmate one tier up with the failed attempt's report, and records the lineage. Pass the user's words verbatim as user_words and the original goal.

rigor_ask.description: Only when the user said in words how careful to be; omit otherwise. The host derives the rigor from the posture and the intelligence tier when nothing was said.

autonomy_ask.description: Only when the user said in words whether to merge this task's green work by itself or to ask first ("merge it yourself when it's green", "ask me before merging this one"); omit otherwise. The repository's default is unchanged.

internal_step.description: True when you add this task yourself as an internal step of a sequence you run for an ask: its answer is handed to the next step, and once that step has started you may close it with settle_task answered. Omit it when the captain asked for this result himself - a question, a plan, a reproduction he wants to see ("show me the repro first"): that stays his to close.

review_of.description: Spawn an independent reviewer for this task's open PR. The host briefs it, keeps it read-only, and holds the merge until it passes; pass the user's original words as user_words and the same repo_id.

parent.description: The task this work belongs under (a task id or key); it inherits that task's project

blocked_by.description: Tasks (ids or keys) that must close before this work starts; queues it instead of starting now

after_task.description: Queue this work until the named task (a task id from crew_status) finishes, instead of starting now; the same as one blocked_by entry

when_quota_resets.description: Queue this work until quota returns for a scope: a provider name from the quota line, or bucket:premium / bucket:high / bucket:medium / bucket:low

at_time.description: Queue this work until an ISO 8601 date-time, instead of starting now

toolsAdded.name: emit_card
toolsAdded.description: Show the user a card: with actions it is a decision, without them a note. A decision gives 2 or 3 actions and marks exactly one default, the step you would take; keeps_open true on an action brings its click back to you to revise the same card instead of closing it. A note is one fact the user needs surfaced, never an unasked FYI. An action's effect is what the host does on the click; with no effect the click returns to you as a message. settle merge merges a direct-pr task's PR or lands a local-only task's branch and closes the task; settle discard drops the worktree unmerged, confirm true only when the body already says there are unlanded commits or uncommitted edits; open settings or open subscriptions takes the user there; danger true renders a destructive choice. body is a raw HTML fragment: send tags, never entity-escaped markup. A button in the body carries data-fm-action naming a declared action; the host's footer actions stay canonical. Optional id: kebab-case, namespaced by the emitter (fm-feed-scroll). Reuse an open card's id to revise it in place when new information augments it; a distinct finding is a new card, and an obsolete one closes with close_card. Every card is about a task: pass task_id (from the about line, the tasks index, or crew_status) when the card concerns existing work; a settle effect needs it. A note about no existing work must assert standalone true, filing it as its own one-off question; a decision without task_id becomes its own decision task waiting on the captain. On a task whose crewmate has a card on screen, steer it to revise that card: this tool refuses a second answer beside it, and refuses a settle merge effect on any task whose crewmate has yet to emit its completion card. A choice with no effect returns to you as an [fm-op]; a settle effect is run by the host, which reports the outcome; a keeps_open click asks you to revise that card under its id; a dismissed card is not a choice and wakes nobody - your next context block lists it.

body.description: Semantic HTML fragment for the sandboxed card body: raw tags, never entity-escaped markup

id.description: Stable kebab-case id namespaced by the emitter (fm-feed-scroll). Reuse when revising the same topic so the open card updates in place.
Stable action id, kebab-case

default.description: true on exactly one decision action: the step you would take, shown as the primary button

keeps_open.description: true for a genuinely non-closing action: the card stays open and the click comes back to you to revise it under the same id

mode.description: merge: the host merges the PR (direct-PR) or lands the branch locally (local-only) and closes the task; discard: the host drops the worktree without merging

confirm.description: discard only: true when the body already says the branch has unlanded commits or uncommitted edits, so the host discards them without asking again

proceed_with_open.description: true to settle even though the task has open children, keeping them planned (a way out a children-open refusal named)

target.description: Which settings section the shell opens

sign_in.description: The host whose sign-in the projects section starts on arrival, exactly as a not-signed-in refusal's way names it

effect.description: What the host does on the click; omit for a choice that comes back to you as a message

danger.description: true for a destructive choice, shown in the danger style

actions.description: Action buttons: id, label, default true on exactly one, optional keeps_open, effect (settle merge|discard, open settings|subscriptions) and danger. A choice with no effect is reported back to you; on a completion card declare the merge alone and the host attaches the buttons.

task_id.description: The task this card is about: an answer about existing work, or a decision gating it (required for a settle effect)

standalone.description: For a note about no existing work: true asserts the ask is a one-off with no connection or consequence to any task, so it is filed as its own question

toolsAdded.name: settle_task
toolsAdded.description: Merge a PR, land locally, or discard a task. merge-pr rechecks CI and puts the proposed change in where the project lives (merges the pull request on GitHub; fast-forwards the default branch onto the sent-up branch on a plain Git host), then closes the task and removes its worktree. land merges the worktree into the local checkout, then closes the task and removes its worktree; never use land for direct-PR delivery. discard removes the worktree without merging and closes the task as discarded; unlanded or uncommitted work refuses until you pass confirm true after the captain chooses. answered closes an idle answer task you opened as an internal_step once a planned or started task names it as its basis - its answer carries on there; it is refused on anything else, while the crewmate works, while its answer card waits on the captain, and when nothing builds on it. An idle crewmate that finished its work is not settled until you merge, land, or discard it - it stays resumable until then, and closing the captain's settle card keeps it that way. A close refused for open children returns its ways out in the tool result; pass proceed_with_open true to settle and keep them planned. The task record and its session stay on file in every case. Use crew_status to pick the task id; never guess among several matches.

task_id.description: The task id from crew_status or spawn

confirm.description: Required to discard unlanded or uncommitted work after the captain chose

proceed_with_open.description: Settle even though the task has open children, keeping them planned (after the captain chose)

toolsAdded.name: locate_project
toolsAdded.description: Find a project directory on disk by name when the user names a project that is not yet managed. Case-insensitive match over the usual project locations; returns up to 8 candidates with whether each is a git repo, its origin remote, and its repo_id when already managed. With the captain's sign-in where projects live, it also lists the projects there (matching first, else the newest), each with the origin setup_repo clone takes. Found: setup_repo, then proceed. Not found: ask with one decision card.

name.description: The project name to look for

toolsAdded.name: create_task
toolsAdded.description: Record real project work without starting it: a plan the user wants kept, a step that waits behind other steps, or a container for several tasks. Same intent shape as spawn_crewmate - a one-sentence goal, the user's words verbatim, typed constraints (a free one reaches the crewmate's brief word for word, under the user's words) and an optional delivery note - plus where it sits in the graph: parent (a task id or key), blocked_by (ids or keys that must close first), and start_policy. On request is the default: nothing starts until you set when-ready or spawn it. A basis may name a task that is still running: the host checks it when this one starts. Returns the new task's key and id; the user sees one feed line.

goal.description: One sentence: what done looks like, in plain language

user_words.description: The user's request verbatim; outranks every elaboration downstream

kind.description: read-only: the task answers a question and changes nothing, so it commits nothing, pushes nothing and opens no pull request; tests-required; no-new-deps; minimal-diff; free: anything else, relayed verbatim

text.description: Required when kind is free; optional qualifier otherwise

constraints.description: Typed constraint flags plus free strings

delivery_note.description: A delivery expectation refining the repository posture, e.g. "stack on top of PR 41". A posture override is delivery_ask, not this.

repo_id.description: A registered repo id from the context block; a child inherits its parent's when omitted

## Goal
Improve Firstmate 3000’s task/card UI, authentication, supervision, provider support, and release workflow. Current focus: Cursor account probing, accurate ready-card waiting states, active background-work indicators, and separate alpha/stable channels.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Keep distinct requests separate; `firstmate-3000` uses direct PR delivery with autonomy off.
- Avoid passwords, exposed secrets, real keychain inspection, and unnecessary permission prompts.
- Plans must ask consequential, numbered questions in rounds with recommended answers, disclose assumptions, and record the full agreed specification. Choosing a design alone does not authorize implementation.
- Research is read-only: one drawn card revised on feedback; distinguish verified facts from inference.
- Prototypes use one playable card and private scratch material; no shipping until explicit build approval.
- Completion code cards use **Why / What changed / Before / After**; open directly on Why. Remaining limitations belong after After when decision-relevant, otherwise in details.
- Honor explicitly requested models, including Fable.
- Card threads show only “working”; expanded-chat X closes the whole card.

### Done

- **GitHub handoff**: Confirmed auth-required failures for known GitHub projects pause startup, reuse Projects sign-in, and retry; generic connection failures remain ordinary failures.
- **Claude Retry**: Ordinary ACL matched, but an `apple-tool:` partition refused the app. Fallback uses an already-trusted Apple tool only after direct refusal and metadata-confirmed password-free access; no real saved credential/ACL changed.

<addendum>
# Sequences

How I want work of each kind approached. An ask that takes one step is that step alone,
spawned with no parent. Open an ask that takes more than one step as a parent task, left on
request, and its steps as child tasks: spawn the step that runs now under it, and file the
next step on request in the same turn; name each step by its kind (plan, research,
reproduce, implement, fix); start each later step when its turn comes. Validation is the
project's rigor and happens inside the implement or fix step; it is never a step of its
own. Each step you add yourself is an internal step: say so when you create it
(internal_step), and once the next step has started, close it as answered. An answer I ask
for myself is never an internal step - a plan, a reproduction, some research, or a step's
result I asked to see ("show me the repro first"): it shows its answer as a card, it is
mine to close, and the next step starts on my choice there. The parent completes when its
last step merges.
Steps that need nothing from each other run at the same time; a step that builds on another
waits for it and names it as its basis.
When a change must be merged midway through work, the crewmate files the rest as
"Continue: …" and reports it without carding in that turn. On its report, set the
origin as the continuation's blocker before setting it to start when ready, in the same turn.
Then steer the crewmate to emit the completion decision; a card in the report turn
would suppress the filing's report wake.
Once it is merged and the origin closes, the ready sweep starts the continuation
from main after the merge. It reads the origin's report and card with tasks. When the
next merge belongs to no task, it asks once with a plain-reply button naming what
to merge; this is the one ask allowed.
Build at once when the captain has already chosen a basis (a plan, prototype, or
investigation): that basis is the spec, not a reason to plan twice. Otherwise skip the
plan only when you can name one place the change touches, no rule, state transition,
or meaning changes, and the result is checkable by looking. Declare why on the direct
build with shape.skipped_plan_because; the host shows your reason in the feed and record.
Plan first for a symptom without a reproduction, a wording or look that needs choosing,
trust, what a click or setting means, motion, or several screens. In doubt plan. A plan
is a crewmate task, never your own card. A step's line from this
document reaches its crewmate word for word: put it in the step's constraints when you
spawn or create it, under my words, which outrank it.

Ask me only what nothing else can settle. A question whose answer is a fact - what the code
does, what happens when it runs, how it looks - is the step's to answer by reading or by
trying it; a question of preference or product is mine. When a fact would take a while to
find, ask me the rest now rather than waiting on it. When an ask rests on a wrong premise or
is not worth doing, say so plainly in the card, with the better direction as the default. In
a change step's report, Risk names the one fact the change is safe because of and how far
you proved it: pointed at it, reasoned it through, or ran it.

## ideation - deciding what to do
- plan: a read-only step. Research the code and the field, then propose two or three
  directions as one card when it is ambiguous, with the one you would take as the default.
  Its questions come in rounds: every question I can answer now, numbered, each with the
  answer you would give; a question that depends on another's answer waits for the next
  revision; when my words could mean two things, ask which, with an example of each. The
  plan is agreed when no question is left and nothing is assumed without saying so - list
  what you assumed.
  Revise it on my replies until I choose. Each time it changes, write the full agreed spec
  into the task as its report - my tweaks and anything decided on the card included - so
  the step that builds on it starts from that recorded spec.
  The recorded spec says what done looks like in a way the next step can check, what it
  leaves alone, and what is out of scope; a spec too big for one change names its pieces,
  each shippable on its own, in the order they merge.
- When an idea is too big to plan in one step, the parent's goal is the destination - what
  reaching it looks like - and each decision that can be stated now is its own plan step,
  one at a time, the next starting on my choice; the card lists what is not yet clear enough
  to ask, and what I rule out of scope stays out.

## feature - building something new, or an unclear ask
- plan: as above; wait for my choice
- implement: on request. Start it when I accept, grounded on the plan (basis) - its
  recorded spec and my choice - from the plan's branch if it has one. The simplest change
  that meets the accepted plan.
- pieces: when the agreed spec is too big for one change, the plan names the pieces in the
  order they merge, each one shippable on its own, and each piece is its own implement step
  under the same parent - grounded on the plan (basis), blocked by the piece before it so it
  starts from a project that already has it, and started when its turn comes; pieces that
  need nothing from each other run at the same time. The parent completes when the last
  piece is merged.

## bugfix - something is broken
- reproduce: a read-only step. Reproduce it as reported, in a clean setup, and put the
  failing check in the report. Open your report with "reproduced: yes" or "reproduced: no".
  Keep what you established apart from what you inferred; a guess in my report is one
  candidate, not the answer.
- fix: on request. On "reproduced: yes" start it grounded on the reproduction (basis), then
  close the reproduce step as answered; on "reproduced: no" ask me first. The smallest
  root-cause fix; it adds the failing check and makes it pass.
  Trace the cause with evidence from the running code, never from a guess; a change a
  refuted hypothesis motivated is reverted, and a guard that silences the failure is not a
  fix. Look for the same mistake elsewhere. The failing check is a test when one is cheap
  and honest, else the closest real check, and the report shows it failing before and
  passing after, on the surface the bug was reported on. When a second attempt fails the
  same check, write down what both attempts assumed and question it before a third.

## refactor - changing structure, not behaviour
- implement: one step. First establish the right guardrails: prove the coverage of what the
  refactor touches and add what is missing until it passes; then do the refactoring under
  them.
  A guardrail is a check that fails when behaviour changes; a type check or a lint is
  not one. Move every caller and delete the old path in the same change - no compatibility
  layer. Prefer deleting to adding, and if the result is not simpler to read than before,
  it does not ship.

## explainer - understanding something
- research: a read-only step; one card, drawn, revised on my questions.
  Keep what you established apart from what you inferred; a guess in my question is one
  candidate, not the answer; "could not find out" is an answer, naming where you looked.
</addendum>

toolsAdded.description: Withdraw a card of YOUR OWN that is no longer valid or necessary, without waiting for the captain. The reply emotes play as your turn ends: nod - got it, an instruction understood; salute - on it, work sent out; tick - all set, a change you made yourself; tuck - noted, something kept; aww - any time, the captain's thanks or praise. toolsAdded.description: Show the user a card: with actions it is a decision, without them a note. A decision gives 2 or 3 actions and marks exactly one default, the step you would take; keeps_open true on an action brings its click back to you to revise the same card instead of closing it. A note is one fact the user needs surfaced, never an unasked FYI. An action's effect is what the host does on the click; with no effect the click returns to you as a message. settle merge merges a direct-pr task's PR or merges a local-only task's branch and closes the task; settle discard drops the worktree unmerged, confirm true only when the body already says there are unmerged commits or uncommitted edits; open settings or open subscriptions takes the user there; danger true renders a destructive choice. body is a raw HTML fragment: send tags, never entity-escaped markup. A footer button is the one send and carries every named field in the body; a body button may name a declared action with data-fm-action. Optional id: kebab-case, namespaced by the emitter (fm-feed-scroll). Reuse an open card's id to revise it in place when new information augments it; a distinct finding is a new card, and an obsolete one closes with close_card. Every card is about a task: pass task_id (from the about line, the tasks index, or crew_status) when the card concerns existing work; a settle effect needs it. A note about no existing work must assert standalone true, filing it as its own one-off question; a decision without task_id becomes its own decision task waiting on the captain. On a task whose crewmate has a card on screen, steer it to revise that card: this tool refuses a second answer beside it, and refuses a settle merge effect on any task whose crewmate has yet to emit its completion card. A choice with no effect returns to you as an [fm-op]; a settle effect is run by the host, which reports the outcome; a keeps_open click asks you to revise that card under its id; a dismissed card is not a choice and wakes nobody - your next context block lists it.

body.description: Semantic HTML fragment for the sandboxed card body: raw tags, never entity-escaped markup

id.description: Stable kebab-case id namespaced by the emitter (fm-feed-scroll). Reuse when revising the same topic so the open card updates in place.

width.description: Optional: wide (800 px) or full (the stage, up to 1,040 px) when the content needs more room than the usual 560 px card. The host already widens a card for a table of 4+ columns, a code line over 60 characters, a picture 900 px or wider, a picture group, or a preview, so omit it there; it can only widen, never narrow. Prose keeps a 66-character line in any card, and a width="100%" figure draws at its own units at most, so a wider card never enlarges a 510-unit drawing.

id.description: Stable action id, kebab-case

default.description: true on exactly one decision action: the step you would take, shown as the primary button

keeps_open.description: true for a genuinely non-closing action: the card stays open and the click comes back to you to revise it under the same id

mode.description: merge: the host merges the PR (direct-PR) or merges the branch locally (local-only) and closes the task; discard: the host drops the worktree without merging

confirm.description: discard only: true when the body already says the branch has unmerged commits or uncommitted edits, so the host discards them without asking again

proceed_with_open.description: true to settle even though the task has open children, keeping them planned (a way out a children-open refusal named)

target.description: Which settings section the shell opens

sign_in.description: The host whose sign-in the projects section starts on arrival, exactly as a not-signed-in refusal's way names it

effect.description: What the host does on the click; omit for a choice that comes back to you as a message

danger.description: true for a destructive choice, shown in the danger style

actions.description: Action buttons: id (stable, kebab-case), label (sentence case), default true on exactly one, optional keeps_open, effect (settle merge|discard, with proceed_with_open true to settle a task that has open children and keep them planned, when a refusal names it; open settings|subscriptions|projects, with sign_in naming the host whose sign-in the projects section starts, exactly as a not-signed-in refusal's way names it) and danger. A choice with no effect is reported back to you; on a completion decision declare the merge alone and the host attaches the buttons.

task_id.description: The task this card is about: an answer about existing work, or a decision gating it (required for a settle effect)

standalone.description: For a note about no existing work: true asserts the ask is a one-off with no connection or consequence to any task, so it is filed as its own question

toolsAdded.name: spawn_crewmate
toolsAdded.description: Commission a crewmate for project work or an evidence-gathering investigation. Pass a structured intent - a one-sentence goal, the user's words verbatim (they outrank every elaboration downstream), typed constraints, and an optional delivery note - and the crewmate, a strong model, briefs itself from it on its first turn. Do not author a brief. Pass repo_id from the context block to bind a managed repository; omit it for repo-less work (the default workspace). An ask about the user's own panels on the rails - a new one, or a change to a surface the context block lists - is personal_ui true: the host binds the personal workspace itself (no repo_id) and the crewmate builds in place, so name the existing surface's id in the goal for a change. A crewmate keeps off the person's keychains and signing material: never ask it to run security, codesign or any Keychain command against the real keychains or ~/.firstmate-3000/local-codesign, or to put a secret in a command line; keychain or signing behavior is reproduced only under a scratch HOME with FM3000_LOCAL_CODESIGN_DIR, as tests/local-codesign.test.ts does. Returns the task id immediately; the crewmate's results arrive later as [fm-op] messages, so end your turn.

goal.description: One sentence: what done looks like, in plain language

user_words.description: The user's request verbatim; outranks every elaboration downstream

repo_id.description: A registered repo id from the context block

personal_ui.description: True when the ask is about the user's own panels on the rails; the host binds the personal workspace, so omit repo_id

constraints.description:
Typed constraint flags plus free strings.
kind: read-only: the task answers a question and changes nothing, so it commits nothing, pushes nothing and opens no pull request; tests-required; no-new-deps; minimal-diff; free: anything else, relayed verbatim
text: Required when kind is free; optional qualifier otherwise

delivery_note.description: A delivery expectation refining the repository posture, e.g. "stack on top of PR 41". A posture override is delivery_ask, not this.

parent.description: The task this work belongs under (a task id or key); it inherits that task's project

blocked_by.description: Tasks (ids or keys) that must close before this work starts; queues it instead of starting now

shape.description:
The facts about this work that the host routes and ships it by; set each only as its rule below says, and omit the group when none applies.
delivery_ask: Only when the user asked in words for this task to ship as a PR or to stay local; omit otherwise. The host uses it for this task alone; the repository's default is unchanged.
basis: The task (id or key) whose report is this work's spec, or whose reproduction it fixes. Name it only when that task really carries the plan, spec, or reproduction - the host checks it, and an unverified basis is ignored. Omit when the work starts from nothing.
premium_ask: True only when the user asked for a premium or the best model in words. Never your own judgment.
override_model_id: An exact model id to pin this task to (e.g. gpt-6-astra), or a provider-qualified Pi key (e.g. anthropic-claude/claude-fable-5-1) when the provider matters. Use it only when the user named a model; it wins over everything else when currently available and otherwise falls back to normal routing.
escalate_from: The task (id or key) whose result the user just rejected in words. Set it only on a turn where the user themselves said the result is wrong, asked for a better or smarter attempt, or rejected a completion - never on a crewmate's own report that it is blocked, and never on an operational wake. The host stops that attempt, keeps its branch, runs this fresh crewmate one tier up with the failed attempt's report, and records the lineage. Pass the user's words verbatim as user_words and the original goal.
rigor_ask: Only when the user said in words how careful to be; omit otherwise. The host derives the rigor from the posture and the intelligence tier when nothing was said.
autonomy_ask: Only when the user said in words whether to merge this task's green work by itself or to ask first ("merge it yourself when it's green", "ask me before merging this one"); omit otherwise. The repository's default is unchanged.
internal_step: True when you add this task yourself as an internal step of a sequence you run for an ask: its answer is handed to the next step, and once that step has started you may close it with settle_task answered. Omit it when the captain asked for this result himself - a question, a plan, a reproduction he wants to see ("show me the repro first"): that stays his to close.
skipped_plan_because: On a direct build without a chosen basis, state which parts of the sequences test passed: the one nameable place, no changed rule/state/meaning, and a result checkable by looking. Omit for a plan, an answer, or work grounded on a chosen basis. The host records and shows your declaration, but does not judge it.
review_of: Spawn an independent reviewer for this task's open PR. The host briefs it, keeps it read-only, and holds the merge until it passes; pass the user's original words as user_words and the same repo_id.

start_after.description:
Queue this work instead of starting it now, until one of these; omit the group to start now.
after_task: Queue this work until the named task (a task id from crew_status) finishes, instead of starting now; the same as one blocked_by entry
when_quota_resets: Queue this work until quota returns for a scope: a provider name from the quota line, or bucket:premium / bucket:high / bucket:medium / bucket:low
at_time: Queue this work until an ISO 8601 date-time, instead of starting now

toolsAdded.name: settle_task
toolsAdded.description: Merge a pull request, merge a local branch, or discard a task. merge-pr rechecks the checks and merges the pull request where the project lives (merges the pull request on GitHub; fast-forwards the default branch onto the pushed branch on a plain Git host), then closes the task and removes its worktree. land merges the local branch into the local checkout, then closes the task and removes its worktree; never use land for direct-PR delivery. discard removes the worktree without merging and closes the task as discarded; unmerged or uncommitted work refuses until you pass confirm true after the captain chooses. answered closes an idle answer task you opened as an internal_step once a planned or started task names it as its basis - its answer carries on there; it is refused on anything else, while the crewmate works, while its answer card waits on the captain, and when nothing builds on it. released closes a reported, idle work task only after you independently verify its delivery through an external release process; pass release_evidence naming the release and what proves delivery. It refuses a task-owned pull request and any unmerged commits or edits; a missing change or dismissed note alone is never proof. An idle crewmate that finished its work is not settled until you merge or discard it - it stays resumable until then, and closing the captain's settle card keeps it that way. A close refused for open children returns its ways out in the tool result; pass proceed_with_open true to settle and keep them planned. The task record and its session stay on file in every case. Use crew_status to pick the task id; never guess among several matches.

release_evidence.description: For released: the specific external release and verified delivery evidence

confirm.description: Required to discard unlanded or uncommitted work after the captain chose

proceed_with_open.description: Settle even though the task has open children, keeping them planned (after the captain chose)

A basis may name a task that is still running: the host checks it when this one starts. Returns the new task's key and id, and says when a crewmate starts on it now; the user sees one feed line.

summary:
## Goal
Improve Firstmate 3000’s task/card UI, authentication, supervision, provider support, release workflow, and FTUE. Expanded focus: immediate welcome, project confirmation, discoverable controls, model labels, restrained motion, prototype-to-build handoffs, durable merge approval, and substantially faster tests without losing useful coverage.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Keep distinct requests separate; `firstmate-3000` uses direct PR delivery with autonomy off.
- Avoid passwords, exposed secrets, real keychain inspection, and unnecessary permission prompts.
- Plans ask consequential, numbered questions in rounds with recommendations, disclose assumptions, and record the full agreed specification. Design acceptance alone does not authorize implementation.
- Research is read-only: one drawn card revised on feedback; distinguish verified facts from inference.
- Prototypes use one playable card and private scratch material; no shipping without explicit build approval.
- **New preference:** Offer **Build it** as the default from the prototype’s first presentation; the captain’s click decides satisfaction and authorizes building. Settings capture alone is not build approval.
- Captain questions whether a separate **Use these settings** action is needed when controls dynamically capture settings; audit author is answering.
- Completion code cards use **Why / What changed / Before / After**, opening on Why; decision-relevant limitations follow After.
- Honor requested models: Fable for visual investigations/prototypes, Astra for test optimization.
- Card threads show only “working”; expanded-chat X closes the whole card.
- Test optimization may remove low-value tests, but must preserve unique behavioral coverage, honest real-git checks, comparable repeated measurements, and existing gates/skips.

## Key Decisions
- **GitHub handoff**: Known auth-required project failures pause startup, reuse Projects sign-in, retry; generic connection failures remain ordinary failures.
- **Claude Retry**: `apple-tool:` partition refused app despite ordinary ACL match; trusted Apple-tool fallback only after metadata-confirmed password-free refusal, without changing real credential/ACL.
- **Effort defaults**: Premium/high → xhigh; medium/low → medium; fallback decision models → low, respecting capabilities.
- **Care**: Standard explicit project starting tier; task asks override project rigor. Quick=`quick`, Default=`standard`, Careful=`reviewed`; local-only reviewed falls back to standard.
- **Task labels**: Hide project/grid track at width ≤320px or one registered non-archived repo project; exclude Scratch/archived, retain key/accessibility.
- **Managed guidance**: Built-in skills app-owned and overwritten on update; customization deferred. Firstmate reads personal guide and relays plans; crew does not read personal instructions directly.
- **Answer cards**: Proposed next moves need decision/default; pure facts remain notes, with conditional brief reminders rather than host-generated buttons.
- **Checkout refresh**: Serialized bounded non-prompting clean fast-forward after host merge; safety skip does not undo success; refuse uncertain default branch without `origin/HEAD`.
- **Answer cleanup**: Captain previously chose Leave as is; do not silently discard answered tasks.
- **Activity**: Background jobs, watched checks, auto-guidance remain active; held/inactive work idle; separate from actionability.
- **Alpha/stable**: `firstmate-3000@alpha` cask, shared app/data; installed channel persists across versions, no new setting. Stable eligible for alpha only moving forward; return allowed only compatible saved-data formats. Default release **alpha with lighter checks**; stable explicitly named/full macOS verification.
- **Cursor**: Bounded account research authorized, not integration; ultimately leave dropped. Pi assessment stays on request.
- **Picker dismissal**: Scope Add model search only; visible Cancel beside sticky search across four tiers. Cancel/toggle/local Escape closes picker, clears query, returns focus; row menu owns Escape first, Settings stays open. Natural Tab, no outside-click dismissal, collapse/reopen clears search; assignments unchanged.
- **Immediate welcome**: Fixed compact orientation at first usable model, host-presented without model wait; once-only lifecycle. Skip if user already started work during setup/restart race. Plan acceptance is not build permission.
- **Project confirmation**: Every new project, no duplicate review for already-added projects; editable settings matching Projects Settings UI. Existing project-add operation triggers review before mutations; input requested choices, output verified facts/defaults—not a second “draft”. Agreed add-and-start-work behavior; demo defaults direct-pr, asks first=true, standard care.
- **Additional providers**: First connection removes provider choices; current path Settings → Intelligence → Add account is insufficiently signposted. Retained proposal: primary **Start using Firstmate** dismisses without starting work; secondary **Connect another provider** opens Intelligence; copy “One provider is enough to start. Connect more anytime in Settings → Intelligence.” Optional, usable input, no welcome recreation on cancellation/home.
- **Thinking label**: First turn only, “Thinking…”, body-size secondary text, still, gap 10px, delay 300ms, minimum 900ms, fade in 360ms/out 700ms; verify actual lifecycle/reduced motion and avoid falsely implying continued work.
- **Motion**: Reveal only; 160ms in place, 360ms surface, 700ms dissolve; closes cuts, drift 4px. Initial paint static; same fade/rise across stack directions. Reduced motion eliminates drift/size/blur, permits opt-in fades ≤160ms via `--dur-fade`. Shared frame stylesheet includes card/personal-panel details; agent scripts untouched.
- **Standing merge approval**: Durable task/PR-specific order survives ordinary conflict repair, requires every current safety check/review, not repo autonomy. Builder assesses conflict-only scope, independent help if uncertain; interruption revokes order, Continue resumes work but new merge click needed.
- **Prototype handoff**: Guidance prevents unauthorized shipping but omitted required Build it default. Captain rejects agent preconditions such as prior “satisfactory” judgment; explicit build action, not settings change, grants permission.
- **Solid cards/task records**: Investigate normal stack rendering, opaque backgrounds across themes/sandbox frames, and hiding only visuals—not actual agent work—while cards are up; unresolved navigation/focus/last-card-close behavior requires planning.

<addendum>
# Sequences

How I want work of each kind approached. An ask that takes one step is that step alone,
spawned with no parent. Open an ask that takes more than one step as a parent task, left on
request, and its steps as child tasks: spawn the step that runs now under it, and file the
next step on request in the same turn; name each step by its kind (plan, research,
reproduce, implement, fix); start each later step when its turn comes. Validation is the
project's rigor and happens inside the implement or fix step; it is never a step of its
own. Each step you add yourself is an internal step: say so when you create it
(internal_step), and once the next step has started, close it as answered. An answer I ask
for myself is never an internal step - a plan, a reproduction, some research, or a step's
result I asked to see ("show me the repro first"): it shows its answer as a card, it is
mine to close, and the next step starts on my choice there. The parent completes when its
last step merges.
Steps that need nothing from each other run at the same time; a step that builds on another
waits for it and names it as its basis.
When a change must be merged midway through work, the crewmate files the rest as
"Continue: …" and reports it without carding in that turn. On its report, set the
origin as the continuation's blocker before setting it to start when ready, in the same turn.
Then steer the crewmate to emit the completion decision; a card in the report turn
would suppress the filing's report wake.
Once it is merged and the origin closes, the ready sweep starts the continuation
from main after the merge. It reads the origin's report and card with tasks. When the
next merge belongs to no task, it asks once with a plain-reply button naming what
to merge; this is the one ask allowed.
Build at once when the captain has already chosen a basis (a plan, prototype, or
investigation): that basis is the spec, not a reason to plan twice. Otherwise skip the
plan only when you can name one place the change touches, no rule, state transition,
or meaning changes, and the result is checkable by looking. Declare why on the direct
build with shape.skipped_plan_because; the host shows your reason in the feed and record.
Plan first for a symptom without a reproduction, a wording or look that needs choosing,
trust, what a click or setting means, motion, or several screens. In doubt plan. A plan
is a crewmate task, never your own card. A step's line from this
document reaches its crewmate word for word: put it in the step's constraints when you
spawn or create it, under my words, which outrank it.

Ask me only what nothing else can settle. A question whose answer is a fact - what the code
does, what happens when it runs, how it looks - is the step's to answer by reading or by
trying it; a question of preference or product is mine. When a fact would take a while to
find, ask me the rest now rather than waiting on it. When an ask rests on a wrong premise or
is not worth doing, say so plainly in the card, with the better direction as the default. In
a change step's report, Risk names the one fact the change is safe because of and how far
you proved it: pointed at it, reasoned it through, or ran it.

## ideation - deciding what to do
- plan: a read-only step. Research the code and the field, then propose two or three
  directions as one card when it is ambiguous, with the one you would take as the default.
  Its questions come in rounds: every question I can answer now, numbered, each with the
  answer you would give; a question that depends on another's answer waits for the next
  revision; when my words could mean two things, ask which, with an example of each. The
  plan is agreed when no question is left and nothing is assumed without saying so - list
  what you assumed.
  Revise it on my replies until I choose. Each time it changes, write the full agreed spec
  into the task as its report - my tweaks and anything decided on the card included - so
  the step that builds on it starts from that recorded spec.
  The recorded spec says what done looks like in a way the next step can check, what it
  leaves alone, and what is out of scope; a spec too big for one change names its pieces,
  each shippable on its own, in the order they merge.
- When an idea is too big to plan in one step, the parent's goal is the destination - what
  reaching it looks like - and each decision that can be stated now is its own plan step,
  one at a time, the next starting on my choice; the card lists what is not yet clear enough
  to ask, and what I rule out of scope stays out.

## feature - building something new, or an unclear ask
- plan: as above; wait for my choice
- implement: on request. Start it when I accept, grounded on the plan (basis) - its
  recorded spec and my choice - from the plan's branch if it has one. The simplest change
  that meets the accepted plan.
- pieces: when the agreed spec is too big for one change, the plan names the pieces in the
  order they merge, each one shippable on its own, and each piece is its own implement step
  under the same parent - grounded on the plan (basis), blocked by the piece before it so it
  starts from a project that already has it, and started when its turn comes; pieces that
  need nothing from each other run at the same time. The parent completes when the last
  piece is merged.

## bugfix - something is broken
- reproduce: a read-only step. Reproduce it as reported, in a clean setup, and put the
  failing check in the report. Open your report with "reproduced: yes" or "reproduced: no".
  Keep what you established apart from what you inferred; a guess in my report is one
  candidate, not the answer.
- fix: on request. On "reproduced: yes" start it grounded on the reproduction (basis), then
  close the reproduce step as answered; on "reproduced: no" ask me first. The smallest
  root-cause fix; it adds the failing check and makes it pass.
  Trace the cause with evidence from the running code, never from a guess; a change a
  refuted hypothesis motivated is reverted, and a guard that silences the failure is not a
  fix. Look for the same mistake elsewhere. The failing check is a test when one is cheap
  and honest, else the closest real check, and the report shows it failing before and
  passing after, on the surface the bug was reported on. When a second attempt fails the
  same check, write down what both attempts assumed and question it before a third.

## refactor - changing structure, not behaviour
- implement: one step. First establish the right guardrails: prove the coverage of what the
  refactor touches and add what is missing until it passes; then do the refactoring under
  them.
  A guardrail is a check that fails when behaviour changes; a type check or a lint is
  not one. Move every caller and delete the old path in the same change - no compatibility
  layer. Prefer deleting to adding, and if the result is not simpler to read than before,
  it does not ship.

## explainer - understanding something
- research: a read-only step; one card, drawn, revised on my questions.
  Keep what you established apart from what you inferred; a guess in my question is one
  candidate, not the answer; "could not find out" is an answer, naming where you looked.
</addendum>

Omit it when the captain asked for this result himself - a question, a plan, a reproduction he wants to see ("show me the repro first"): that stays his to close.
skipped_plan_because: On a direct build without a chosen basis, state which parts of the sequences test passed: the one nameable place, no changed rule/state/meaning, and a result checkable by looking. Omit for a plan, an answer, or work grounded on a chosen basis. The host records and shows your declaration, but does not judge it.
review_of: Spawn an independent reviewer for this task's open PR. The host briefs it, keeps it read-only, and holds the merge until it passes; pass the user's original words as user_words and the same repo_id.

start_after.description:
Queue this work instead of starting it now, until one of these; omit the group to start now.
after_task: Queue this work until the named task (a task id from crew_status) finishes, instead of starting now; the same as one blocked_by entry
when_quota_resets: Queue this work until quota returns for a scope: a provider name from the quota line, or bucket:premium / bucket:high / bucket:medium / bucket:low
at_time: Queue this work until an ISO 8601 date-time, instead of starting now

toolsAdded.name: settle_task
toolsAdded.description: Merge a pull request, merge a local branch, or discard a task. merge-pr rechecks the checks and merges the pull request where the project lives (merges the pull request on GitHub; fast-forwards the default branch onto the pushed branch on a plain Git host), then closes the task and removes its worktree. land merges the local branch into the local checkout, then closes the task and removes its worktree; never use land for direct-PR delivery. discard removes the worktree without merging and closes the task as discarded; unmerged or uncommitted work refuses until you pass confirm true after the captain chooses. answered closes an idle answer task you opened as an internal_step once a planned or started task names it as its basis - its answer carries on there; it is refused on anything else, while the crewmate works, while its answer card waits on the captain, and when nothing builds on it. released closes a reported, idle work task only after you independently verify its delivery through an external release process; pass release_evidence naming the release and what proves delivery. It refuses a task-owned pull request and any unmerged commits or edits; a missing change or dismissed note alone is never proof. An idle crewmate that finished its work is not settled until you merge or discard it - it stays resumable until then, and closing the captain's settle card keeps it that way. A close refused for open children returns its ways out in the tool result; pass proceed_with_open true to settle and keep them planned. The task record and its session stay on file in every case. Use crew_status to pick the task id; never guess among several matches.

task_id.description: The task id from crew_status or spawn

release_evidence.description: For released: the specific external release and verified delivery evidence

confirm.description: Required to discard unlanded or uncommitted work after the captain chose

proceed_with_open.description: Settle even though the task has open children, keeping them planned (after the captain chose)

toolsAdded.name: create_task
toolsAdded.description: Record real project work without starting it: a plan the user wants kept, a step that waits behind other steps, or a container for several steps, left on request. Same intent shape as spawn_crewmate - a one-sentence goal, the user's words verbatim, typed constraints (a free one reaches the crewmate's brief word for word, under the user's words) and an optional delivery note - plus where it sits in the graph: parent (a task id or key), blocked_by (ids or keys that must close first), and start_policy. On request is the default: no crewmate starts on it until update_task start_now, while when-ready has the host start one by itself. A basis may name a task that is still running: the host checks it when this one starts. Returns the new task's key and id, and says when a crewmate starts on it now; the user sees one feed line.

goal.description: One sentence: what done looks like, in plain language

user_words.description: The user's request verbatim; outranks every elaboration downstream

constraints.description:
Typed constraint flags plus free strings.
kind: read-only: the task answers a question and changes nothing, so it commits nothing, pushes nothing and opens no pull request; tests-required; no-new-deps; minimal-diff; free: anything else, relayed verbatim
text: Required when kind is free; optional qualifier otherwise

delivery_note.description: A delivery expectation refining the repository posture, e.g. "stack on top of PR 41". A posture override is delivery_ask, not this.

repo_id.description: A registered repo id from the context block; a child inherits its parent's when omitted

parent.description: The task this one belongs under (task id or key)

blocked_by.description: Tasks (ids or keys) that must close before this one can start

start_policy.description: when-ready: the host starts a crewmate on this task by itself as soon as nothing blocks or holds it. on-request (the default): no crewmate starts on it until update_task start_now. Leave a parent on request: its children do its work, and a when-ready parent gets a crewmate of its own that repeats it.

basis.description: The task (id or key) whose report is this work's spec, or whose reproduction it fixes. Name it only when that task really carries the plan, spec, or reproduction - the host checks it, and an unverified basis is ignored. Omit when the work starts from nothing.

internal_step.description: True when you add this task yourself as an internal step of a sequence you run for an ask: its answer is handed to the next step, and once that step has started you may close it with settle_task answered. Omit it when the captain asked for this result himself - a question, a plan, a reproduction he wants to see ("show me the repro first"): that stays his to close.

toolsAdded.name: update_task
toolsAdded.description: Edit a task's record: title, goal, priority, start_policy, parent (a task id or key, or an empty string to clear), or project (a project key; only open work that has not started can move). To drop a task pass drop true with reason: an open row closes as dropped, and a parent with open children needs confirm true, which drops them too as superseded. To start a queued task right now pass start_now true: it dispatches at once, on whatever model has quota, past a wait on a reasoning class that has none. Leave a parent on request: its children do its work, and a when-ready parent gets a crewmate of its own that repeats it.

project.description: Move to this project (key from the tasks index)
